q-56845.name: Question 1
q-56845.worked_solution:
First, we write $10$ as an improper fraction:

$$
10=\frac{10}{1}
$$

Finally, we simplify:

$$
10÷10=1
$$

q-70169.name: Question 2
q-70169.worked_solution:
To multiply a fraction by a whole number, we multiply the fraction's numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same:

$$
\frac{5\times 8}{12}=\frac{40}{12}
$$

We then simplify:

$$
\frac{40}{12}=\frac{40÷4}{12÷4}=\frac{10}{3}
$$

Finally, we then convert $\frac{10}{3}$ to a mixed number:

$$
10÷3=3\,\text{R}1=3\,\frac{1}{3}
$$

q-172835.name: Question 3
q-172835.problem: Expressed as a fraction in its lowest terms, $\frac{2}{9}\times 3=${{field-1}}.
q-172835.worked_solution:
To multiply a fraction by a whole number, we multiply the fraction's numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same:

$$
\frac{2\times 3}{9}=\frac{6}{9}
$$

We then reduce this fraction to its lowest terms:

$$
\frac{6}{9}=\frac{6÷3}{9÷3}=\frac{2}{3}
$$
